note: One-line venue profiles keyed by source NAME (the exact string the classifier receives). Fed to the tagger as a prior — for thin/empty event descriptions the venue type is often the strongest signal (a film at Balboa is a screening; a show at the Fillmore is a concert). Add an entry when adding a source.

profiles.SFJAZZ Center: Jazz concert hall in SF's Hayes Valley; nearly all events are live jazz and adjacent music concerts.
profiles.The Fillmore: Historic SF live-music venue; rock, pop, indie, hip-hop, and electronic concerts.
profiles.The Warfield: Large SF music theater; rock, pop, hip-hop, and comedy concerts/tours.
profiles.Great American Music Hall: SF live-music hall; rock, indie, folk, jazz, and eclectic concerts.
profiles.The Independent: SF (Divisadero) live-music club; indie, rock, electronic, and hip-hop concerts.
profiles.Phoenix Theater (Petaluma): All-ages Petaluma music venue; punk, metal, rock, and hardcore shows.
profiles.City Lights Booksellers: Landmark SF bookstore and publisher (Beat legacy); author talks, readings, and literary events.
profiles.Green Apple Books: Beloved SF bookstore; author talks, readings, and book launches.
profiles.Black Bird Bookstore: Small SF (Outer Sunset) neighborhood bookstore; readings, writing circles, book clubs, and community events.
profiles.Bird & Beckett: Glen Park bookstore known for its live jazz series and poetry readings.
profiles.Medicine for Nightmares: Mission District bookstore and gallery centering Latino/Chicano culture; readings, art openings, and community events.
profiles.A.C.T. (American Conservatory Theater): Major SF nonprofit theater company; plays and musicals (drama, contemporary, classic).
profiles.Berkeley Repertory Theatre: Tony-winning Berkeley nonprofit theater; plays and new works (drama, musicals).
profiles.Magic Theatre: SF (Fort Mason) theater dedicated to new plays by living playwrights.
profiles.New Conservatory Theatre Center: SF nonprofit theater with an LGBTQ+ focus; plays, musicals, and cabaret.
profiles.San Francisco Playhouse: SF downtown nonprofit theater; plays and musicals.
profiles.Brava Theater Center: SF (Mission) theater centering women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ artists; plays, performance, music, and community events.
profiles.Presidio Theatre: Restored SF (Presidio) live-arts venue; a wide mix of theater, music, film, dance, comedy, and speakers.
profiles.Z Space: SF (Mission) contemporary performing-arts venue; new theater, experimental performance, and dance.
profiles.SF Neo-Futurists: SF experimental theater troupe; fast-paced original short-play shows (e.g. The Infinite Wrench).
profiles.Great Star Theater: Historic SF Chinatown performing-arts venue; comedy, variety, karaoke game shows, Chinese opera, and community events.
profiles.Palace of Fine Arts Theatre: Large SF live-event venue; a diverse mix of comedy tours, live podcasts, music, dance, and film presentations.
profiles.Herbst / Davies (SF War Memorial): SF War Memorial venues (Herbst Theatre, Davies Symphony Hall, Opera House); classical concerts, opera, ballet, recitals, lectures, and civic events.
profiles.ATG (Curran, Orpheum, Golden Gate): SF's major touring-Broadway houses (Curran, Orpheum, Golden Gate); big musicals, plays, and large-scale touring shows.
profiles.Balboa Theatre: SF (Outer Richmond) repertory/independent movie theater; film screenings (new releases, classics, repertory).
profiles.4-Star Theater: SF (Inner Richmond) independent movie theater; film screenings, plus occasional live music and events.
profiles.Yerba Buena Center for the Arts: SF contemporary-art center; visual-art exhibitions, film, dance, music, and performance across disciplines.
profiles.San Francisco Public Library: SF public library system; free programs across branches — talks, workshops, book clubs, film, and community activities.
profiles.Big Brain Lectures — Bay Area: Bay Area lecture series; accessible expert talks on science, culture, and ideas at bars and small venues.
profiles.Commonwealth Club: The Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California — the nation's oldest public-affairs forum; nonpartisan talks, panels, and onstage interviews on politics, science, health, climate, and culture.
profiles.City Arts & Lectures: SF nonprofit presenting onstage conversations and lectures (mostly at the Sydney Goldstein Theater); interviews with authors, scientists, artists, and public figures.
profiles.The Riptide: Classic Ocean Beach / Outer Sunset neighborhood bar; nightly free events — live music, DJs, karaoke, bar trivia, bingo, and open mics.
profiles.SF Bar Guide: Directory of recurring weekly SF bar nights aggregated across ~90 bars; each event is a recurring bar night — trivia, karaoke, bingo, drag, comedy, or live music — at a named venue.
profiles.Sunset Trivia: A pub-quiz operator running weekly bar trivia across Bay Area venues; every event is a trivia / quiz night at a named bar.
profiles.The Commons (SF): SF membership community/club (thesfcommons.org); member events — talks, socials, workshops, and gatherings, often around tech, ideas, and community.
profiles.Drake's Brewing: East Bay craft brewery taprooms (Drake's Dealership in Oakland, Barrel House in San Leandro); trivia nights, drag bingo, Lotería, live music, markets.
profiles.Paramount Theatre: Historic art-deco theater in downtown Oakland; Oakland Symphony and Oakland Ballet performances, classic film screenings, comedy, touring concerts.
profiles.Oakland Public Library: Oakland's public library system (Main Library and neighborhood branches); free talks, book clubs, film screenings, art labs, crafts, games, yoga and teen programs.
profiles.Oakland Asian Cultural Center: Asian American cultural center in Oakland Chinatown; author talks, community conversations, workshops, mending circles and performances.
profiles.Oakland United Beerworks: Brewery taproom near Jack London Square, Oakland; paint-and-sip nights, craft workshops, maker markets and seasonal parties.
profiles.EastSide Arts Alliance: East Oakland cultural center (International Blvd); film screenings, book clubs, youth arts workshops, Día de los Muertos and community rituals.
profiles.Bay Area Fusion Calendar: Community calendar of fusion partner dance (blues, zouk, west coast swing, tango fusion) around the Bay Area: weekly and monthly social dances with lessons, workshops and dance weekends.
profiles.Masala Comedy Club: South Bay desi stand-up comedy club; Hindi/English (Hinglish) stand-up shows at theaters around the Bay Area (Sunnyvale, Campbell, San Mateo, Danville) plus a bi-weekly open mic in Milpitas.
profiles.Mission Fusion: SF fusion partner-dance social (first & third Saturdays at St. Gregory of Nyssa, Potrero Hill); an all-levels dance class followed by a DJ'd social dance, sliding-scale entry.
profiles.The Berkeley Alembic: West Berkeley contemplative/community center; meditation, movement and dance (5Rhythms, qigong), breathwork, integration circles, kirtan and devotional music, and talks on consciousness, psychedelics, and spirituality.
profiles.Frontier Tower: SF (Mid-Market, 995 Market St) member-run tech/science hub in a 16-floor tower; talks, hackathons, AI/crypto/neuro meetups, reading groups, and member socials.
profiles.Reading Rhythms: "Reading party" series (not a book club) — attendees read together to live music and curated playlists at bars and cafes; California calendar spans SF Bay Area and LA.
profiles.Oakland Art Murmur: Coalition of Oakland galleries (First Friday art walks); gallery exhibitions, opening receptions, and art-related events.
profiles.El Rio: SF Mission District dive bar and queer/Latinx community venue; live music, DJ dance parties, karaoke, drag, comedy, and patio movie nights.
profiles.Kronos Quartet: Pioneering SF-based string quartet (contemporary/experimental classical); touring concert performances at Bay Area concert halls like Herbst Theatre and Stanford's Bing Concert Hall.
profiles.Litquake: SF's annual literary festival (Litquake); readings, author panels, lit crawls, and spoken-word events across Bay Area venues each fall.
profiles.The Marsh: SF (Mission) and Berkeley venue for solo performance and new theater; one-person shows, storytelling, comedy, staged readings, and music.
profiles.Alonzo King LINES Ballet: Acclaimed SF contemporary ballet company; performances at Bay Area venues (Davies Symphony Hall, Dominican University) plus touring.
profiles.FACT/SF: SF contemporary dance company and studio; dance performances, festivals, works-in-progress showings, and movement classes.
profiles.Yoshi's: Legendary Oakland jazz club and Japanese restaurant; live music concerts (jazz, soul, R&B, funk, world), often multiple nightly sets.
profiles.Keys Jazz Bistro: North Beach SF jazz club/supper club; live jazz concerts (often two sets a night), vocalists, and combos.
profiles.The Dawn Club: Downtown SF jazz club; live jazz, swing, and blues performances (concerts).
profiles.Biscuits & Blues: Union Square SF blues & jazz supper club; live blues, soul, and R&B concerts (with dinner service).
profiles.Bach Dancing & Dynamite Society: Longtime jazz concert series at the Douglas Beach House on Miramar Beach, Half Moon Bay; Sunday-afternoon performances by touring jazz artists (trios, quartets, vocalists).
profiles.The Booksmith: Haight-Ashbury SF independent bookstore; author talks, book launches, and literary/drag performance nights.
profiles.Book Passage: Bay Area independent bookstore (Corte Madera + SF Ferry Building); author talks, book signings, cooking/travel talks, and writing classes/workshops.
profiles.Noe Valley Books: SF Noe Valley neighborhood bookstore; readings, book clubs, poetry open mics, and community events.
profiles.Mrs. Dalloway's: Berkeley (Elmwood) independent bookstore; author readings, book launches, and picture-book events.
profiles.Bookshop West Portal: SF West Portal neighborhood bookstore; author events, book clubs, kids' story time, and community events.
profiles.Clio's Books: Oakland (Grand Lake) independent bookstore focused on history, politics, and ideas; author talks, conversations, and multi-week reading seminars.
profiles.Russian Hill Bookstore: SF Russian Hill (Polk St) neighborhood bookstore; community events such as typewriter poetry and writing workshops, readings.
Bay Area independent bookstore chain (SF, Alameda, Peninsula, South Bay stores); author talks, book clubs, craft workshops, and kids' storytimes.
profiles.Omnivore Books on Food: SF cookbook and food-writing bookstore; cookbook author talks, book signings, and food/drink conversations (occasionally off-site dinners).
profiles.Fabulosa Books: SF Castro queer-focused independent bookstore; LGBTQ+ author readings, book launches, and literary events.
profiles.Tally Ho! Books: Oakland (Piedmont Ave) independent bookstore; author readings, conversations, and book-launch events.
profiles.Partiful: Partiful's public SF discovery feed of community-hosted events: social meetups, walks and hikes, run clubs, book clubs, crafts and workshops, markets, parties, and small shows — hosted by individuals and small groups rather than venues.
profiles.Community submissions: Events emailed in by people in the community — anything from house shows, readings and meetups to venue events; judge each on its own title and description.
profiles.The Faight Collective: Lower Haight community venue, gallery and studio (475 Haight St); live music, DJ nights, open mics, comedy and dating shows, community and art events.
profiles.Artists' Television Access: SF Mission District artist-run microcinema and gallery (992 Valencia); experimental and underground film screenings (Other Cinema, Analogica), film-festival programs, open screenings, and occasional performances.
profiles.Yerba Buena Gardens Festival: Free outdoor performing-arts festival in SF's Yerba Buena Gardens (May–Oct); music concerts, dance performances and participatory dance classes, cultural festivals, and family events.
profiles.Oakland Museum of California: Oakland museum of California art, history and natural science (OMCA); Friday Nights (music, food trucks), gallery talks, architecture walks, exhibition programs, and family days.
profiles.JCCSF: Jewish Community Center of San Francisco (Laurel Heights); author talks and conversations, food and cookbook events, music, film, lectures, and community gatherings.
profiles.Fort Mason Center: SF Marina waterfront arts campus; gallery exhibitions (often long-running), festivals, performances, food and drink events, and a weekly farmers market.
profiles.The Masonic: SF Nob Hill 3,300-seat concert hall (Live Nation); touring pop/rock/indie concerts, comedians, and speaking tours.
profiles.Cobb's Comedy Club: SF North Beach stand-up comedy club (Live Nation); nearly all events are live stand-up comedy shows by touring and local comedians.
profiles.Punch Line San Francisco: SF Financial District stand-up comedy club (Live Nation); nearly all events are live stand-up comedy shows.
profiles.GLBT Historical Society: SF Castro queer history museum and archive; history talks, film screenings, walking tours, workshops, exhibition openings, and community events.
profiles.San Francisco Center for the Book: SF Potrero Hill book-arts center; artists' book exhibitions and opening receptions, artist talks, readings, and letterpress/bookbinding events.
profiles.San Francisco Maritime National Park Ass: SF waterfront maritime-history nonprofit (USS Pampanito at Pier 45, Hyde Street Pier); sea-chantey sings, ship tours, Fleet Week viewing, and fundraising galas.
profiles.Mechanics' Institute: Historic downtown SF membership library and chess club (57 Post St); author talks, classic-film screenings (Movies at Mechanics'), chamber music, seminars, reading groups, writers' groups, and chess lectures.
profiles.Oakland Theater Project: Oakland nonprofit theater company performing at FLAX art & design downtown; plays (classics and new work), staged readings, and music/storytelling evenings.
profiles.The Henry J. Kaiser Center for the Arts: Oakland Lake Merritt arts center (Calvin Simmons Theater, ballrooms); concerts, comedy, family shows, community celebrations, watch parties, and touring exhibitions.
profiles.F8: SF SoMa nightclub (1192 Folsom St); DJ dance parties most nights: house, techno, afro house, darkwave and queer/community club nights.
profiles.Diaspora Arts Connection: Bay Area nonprofit presenting diaspora artists (Persian, Afghan and other immigrant communities); concerts, theater productions, film screenings and cultural celebrations at venues around the Bay Area.
profiles.Stanford Live: Stanford University's performing-arts presenter (Bing Concert Hall, Frost Amphitheater, Dinkelspiel); classical, jazz, world and pop concerts, dance, comedy, and Department of Music student ensembles.
profiles.The Castro Theatre: SF Castro historic movie palace run by Another Planet; concerts, comedy and speaking tours, film screenings and festivals, drag and LGBTQ+ community events.
profiles.Fox Theater Oakland: Oakland Uptown 2,800-capacity concert hall (Another Planet); touring rock, indie, hip-hop and electronic concerts, plus comedy.
profiles.The Greek Theatre Berkeley: UC Berkeley's 8,500-seat outdoor amphitheater (Another Planet); large touring concerts, spring through fall.
profiles.Bimbo's 365 Club: SF North Beach 1930s supper-club ballroom booked by Another Planet; touring indie, rock, soul and jazz concerts, plus drag and comedy shows.
profiles.August Hall: SF Union Square concert venue; touring rock, indie, electronic and hip-hop concerts and DJ nights.
profiles.Feinstein's at the Nikko: SF cabaret and supper club in Hotel Nikko; Broadway and jazz vocalists, tribute and songbook shows, open mics, and Sunday brunch concerts.
profiles.Cal Performances: UC Berkeley's performing-arts presenter (Zellerbach Hall, Hertz Hall); classical and chamber music, dance, theater, jazz and world music, and author/speaker talks.
profiles.The UC Theatre: Berkeley nonprofit 1,400-capacity music hall; touring rock, indie, metal, hip-hop and electronic concerts.
profiles.Roxie Theater: SF Mission nonprofit repertory cinema; film screenings: new independent and international releases, classics, cult and genre series, documentaries, and festivals, often with Q&As.
